active_investigations.title: What would it take to understand the need?
active_investigations.introduction: We're investigating where Stockton's street dogs are, what condition they're in, what care reaches them, and which needs remain unmet. Public reports are starting points; records, firsthand observations, and conversations with responders can help us verify what is happening.
active_investigations.findings_summary: Stockton's municipal shelter handles thousands of stray dog intake events, yet the number of dogs currently on the streets and what happens after a dog is reported remain unclear. Our first attempts to volunteer with two animal-care organizations have not yet led to completed onboarding, raising questions about how easily willing residents can get involved. Meanwhile, shelter expansion is underway and additional facilities are proposed, but their impact on access to care remains to be established.
active_investigations.purpose: Not every dog can immediately be rescued or placed in a home. Until that happens, food, water, emergency medical attention, and people willing to monitor their wellbeing can prevent suffering and potentially save lives.

questions.title: Where are the stray dogs, and how many are there?
questions.description: Can we obtain reliable population estimates and identify where dogs are likely to be found? How current and accurate are the available reports?

questions.title: What condition are they in?
questions.description: Are dogs healthy, hungry, injured, or seriously ill? Can we determine how many need immediate attention?

questions.title: Who is already caring for them?
questions.description: What care do Stockton Streetdogs, Animal Services, and others provide? Can we establish which dogs are receiving help and which aren't?

questions.title: What happens when someone reports a dog?
questions.description: Who receives the report, what action follows, and can we establish what ultimately happens to the animal?

questions.title: What would it take to meet their needs?
questions.description: Do we need more rescue capacity, veterinary care, feeding, transport, or volunteers? What evidence would tell us where additional resources should go?

verification_avenues.title: Field visits and firsthand observations
verification_avenues.description: Check dated reports from safe public areas. Record when and where we looked, what we observed or did not observe, visible condition, and signs of existing care. A single visit cannot establish conditions across a neighborhood.

verification_avenues.title: Contact with responders, caregivers, and organizations
verification_avenues.description: Ask what care they provide, how they respond to reports, what help is useful, and how residents can participate safely. Record a contact attempt separately from a reply or a confirmed result.

verification_avenues.title: Official records and public-source research
verification_avenues.description: Review dated reporting and request Animal Services field-call data. Check each source's coverage and limits; shelter intake totals are not a count of dogs currently on Stockton streets.

verification_avenues.title: Cross-checking evidence and tracing outcomes
verification_avenues.description: Compare reports, records, conversations, and observations. Distinguish a sighting or request from a response, care delivered, reunification, placement, or a resolved need.

observation_fields: Original report or reason for visiting
Evidence of food, water, caregivers, or rescue activity
Direct conversations, recorded with privacy safeguards
result_options: Dogs observed, no visible immediate distress
fieldwork_plan.report_outline: After a visit, publish a short field report stating the general areas visited, what was and was not seen, what was learned, what remains uncertain, and the next action. A single visit does not establish neighborhood-wide conditions. No dogs observed is a valid finding.

contact_plan.intro: These are questions to take to organizations already involved in animal care. Public pages describe services and ways to participate, but they do not establish current unmet needs, safe assignments, or the outcome of a particular report.
shared_checks: For each contact, record the attempt, any reply, what the person or organization reports, and what can be checked independently.

Ask whether a willing resident can find a verified, safe way to help with feeding, supplies, transport, temporary care, or fostering; document geographic or scheduling gaps, onboarding time, requirements, and barriers without creating an unapproved route.

Trace whether a reported need led to qualified assessment, lawful care, reunification or placement, and a confirmed outcome. Protect precise locations and do not approach unfamiliar dogs without appropriate precautions.

records_request.status: Automatic forwarding acknowledgment received; substantive response and records pending as of October 30
records_request.summary: Crossover requested approximately 12 months of Stockton Animal Services field-call records involving roaming, stray, abandoned, aggressive, and distressed dogs. Requested fields include dates, general areas, complaint categories, response dispositions, and closure statuses where maintained.
records_request.review_plan: When records arrive, examine concentrations and repeat reports by general area; separate confirmed pickups, unresolved calls, and other dispositions; compare them with published reports and field observations; and cite any generalized map locations. Availability of requested fields is unknown.

care_coordination.title: Community Care Coordination
care_coordination.central_question: Can ordinary residents identify an unmet need and contribute to safe animal care without unnecessary administrative barriers?
care_coordination.participation_scope: Investigate how willing residents access verified opportunities for observation, supplies, transport, temporary care, fostering, and animal welfare support. Public donation and application links exist; specific assignments, eligibility, response times, and unmet needs require confirmation with the responsible organizations.

public_source_review.summary: The reviewed public pages describe existing feeding and care, donation wishlists, and volunteer or contact entry points. This limited review did not establish a public feeding route, resident safety protocol, supply drop site, or a current request for additional route volunteers. Confirm these directly with responders before publishing instructions.

sources.label: Hungry Tailz Rescue care and contact

questions: If a resident wants to help feed street dogs, can anyone direct them to a verified, safe, existing opportunity? If not, what information, coordination, or capacity is missing?
Which responding organizations coordinate food and water, and do they publish instructions for residents?
Can residents join established feeding or supply routes without duplicating existing work?
What supplies are useful, and where should they be delivered?
Who can evaluate medical urgency and arrange veterinary referrals?
Are there geographic or scheduling gaps that additional volunteers could cover?
Can volunteers transport animals or supplies, provide temporary care, or foster? What qualifications or approvals are required, and how long does onboarding take?
What prevents a willing resident from contributing to established care, and how long does participation take?
What do Stockton Streetdogs and Stockton Animal Services say they provide, and what can be confirmed through direct contact or case evidence?
Can temporary care, reunification, transport, veterinary coordination, and lawful placement be arranged through qualified responders?
What evidence would show that a specific need was resolved rather than only reported or acted upon?
How can people help safely without attracting dogs into traffic, disrupting caregivers, or approaching unfamiliar dogs?

decentralized_protocol_concept.note: This is a proposed workflow, not an operating service. No public live animal-location pins, public claimable rescue assignments, volunteer dispatch, or unattended automated rescue decisions are proposed for this investigation.

care_coordination.capability_note: These are proposed capabilities that may operate concurrently, not required steps or staffed services. Animal reporting, ownership, holding, safety, and veterinary requirements still apply.
care_coordination.potential_outcome: Publish an organization-verified guide to helping street dogs once responders confirm needs, contacts, safe instructions, and any participation requirements.

safeguards: Do not publish precise locations of vulnerable people or animals without a specific reason and consideration of their safety.
Do not assume dogs accompanying unhoused people are stray, abandoned, or neglected.
Do not approach or feed unfamiliar dogs without appropriate safety precautions and coordination.
active_investigations.public_approach: We protect the locations and privacy of vulnerable people and animals. We don't assume dogs accompanying unhoused people are abandoned or neglected. We approach unfamiliar dogs only with appropriate safety precautions and coordination.
active_investigations.known_so_far: Stockton Streetdogs reports increased dumped-dog encounters and conducts street-level assistance. Animal Services publishes reporting routes and, according to October 20 reporting, describes regular shelter capacity pressure, appointment-based healthy stray intake, priority for urgent and confirmed abandonment cases, and a temporary found-animal foster option. These are attributed public statements, not Crossover field observations or verified outcome measures. A roaming dog may be owned, lost, abandoned, or unowned. Stockton’s current street-dog population, severe suffering, care coverage, and individual outcomes remain unknown.

uncertainties: How often dogs on the street are severely underweight, injured, ill, or dying.
Which dogs receive reliable food, water, monitoring, or emergency veterinary care.
Whether responsible caregivers need more coordinated people, supplies, or transport, and whether residents can find clear instructions for participating.
How quickly does Stockton Animal Services respond to reports of roaming dogs, and how are urgent cases prioritized?
Are repeated roaming-dog reports concentrated in particular areas, and what prevents dogs from receiving timely assistance?

illustrative_outcome.title: Possible result: Additional feeding assistance needed
illustrative_outcome.description: An authorized rescue or caregiver confirms that additional people are needed to support a regular feeding route.

active_investigations.opportunity_rule: Practical opportunities should be published only after the responsible organization or caregiver confirms the need, requirements, and appropriate coordination.
active_investigations.short_focus: First street-condition observation pending; reported shelter practices and foster pathway need case-level verification

Review dated Louis Park and Stanislaus Street leads, then complete and record a safe public-area observation, including zero dogs if that is what is seen. Separately follow up on field-call records, volunteer applications, the found-animal foster pathway, and Council consideration of the proposed ordinance.

established_findings.title: Shelter expansion construction was underway on October 14, 2026.
established_findings.summary: Crossover observed construction during its field visit. Completion, usable additional dog-care capacity, and resulting outcomes remain unverified.
